info.title: UltraV API
info.description:
UltraV is a modern, simple, API-first management layer for KVM/QEMU
virtual machines on single Linux hosts.

**Everything is an API.** Every UI capability is available here first.
This contract is the source of truth for the Web UI, CLI, scripts,
automation, and future AI agents (MCP adapters).

## Conventions
- All requests/responses are JSON.
- Every response includes an `X-Request-Id` header; errors also include `requestId` in the body.
- Errors use a stable envelope: `{"error": {"code", "message", "requestId"}}`.
- Destructive or long-running operations will use specific, semantically
  named operations (never generic `execute`/`command` endpoints).

post.summary: Authenticate and obtain a bearer token
post.description: Validates credentials against the local user database (SQLite) and returns a signed JWT bearer token. All other endpoints (except /health and /ready) require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

put.summary: Change the authenticated user's own password

error.message: A user with this username already exists

delete.description: Requires the `admin` role. The caller cannot delete itself and the last remaining admin cannot be deleted.

409.description: Cannot delete self or the last admin

error.message: Cannot delete the last admin user

get.description: Returns status and identity of the hypervisor host.
Feature discovery for UI, automation and agents. Clients must use this to know what the host supports instead of hardcoding assumptions.
Checks only that the application process is alive. Always returns 200 while the process is up.
Checks that the application and the HypervisorProvider are ready to serve requests.

post.description:
Defines, builds and starts a new directory-based storage pool.
The target directory is created if it does not exist.

409.description: A pool with this name already exists

error.message: A storage pool with this name already exists

post.description: Re-syncs the pool's volume list and usage numbers with the backing storage.

get.summary: List ISO images in the library
get.description:
ISO images available as installation media. Backed by a dedicated
directory on the host (ULTRAV_ISO_DIR). Files are uploaded via the
browser with `uploadIso`.

post.description: Streams the file into the ISO library. The filename must end in `.iso`.

409.description: An ISO with this filename already exists

delete.description: Removes the file from the ISO library.

post.description:
Creates a virtual network in one of three modes:
- `nat`: routed + NAT subnet managed by libvirt (DHCP + dnsmasq)
- `bridge`: passthrough to an existing host bridge (VMs get IPs on the
  host's LAN; requires a bridge such as br0 configured on the host --
  libvirt cannot create host bridges)
- `isolated`: internal-only subnet, no outside connectivity

400.description: Invalid input (missing bridgeName for bridge mode, bad CIDR, ...)

409.description: A network with this name already exists

get.description:
Host Linux bridges (e.g. br0) that virtual networks in `bridge` mode can
attach to. Creating these bridges is host configuration (netplan /
NetworkManager), not something libvirt or UltraV does; use this list to
detect what exists and guide the user when nothing is available.

post.description:
Stops the virtual network. Running VMs attached to it keep working but
lose new DHCP leases and NAT until the network is started again.

Defines a new virtual machine: allocates a disk volume in the chosen
storage pool and defines the domain (left stopped unless `start` is
true). The VM is not booted from an OS image — attach installation
media with virt-install/virt-manager afterwards if needed.

409.description: A virtual machine with this name already exists

post.description: Powers on a stopped virtual machine. Returns 409 if already running.

get.description:
Upgrades the connection to a WebSocket and proxies binary frames to the
VM's graphical console (VNC/RFB). The browser side is a noVNC client;
binary messages are raw VNC octets. Requires a running VM (409 otherwise).
Note: this endpoint is a WebSocket — OpenAPI cannot fully describe the
upgraded protocol.

101.description: Switching Protocols — WebSocket established, frames are raw VNC

post.summary: Gracefully shut down a virtual machine
post.description: Sends an ACPI shutdown event. The guest OS should shut down cleanly.
Sends an ACPI reboot event. Returns 409 if the VM is not running.

Immediately powers off the VM, equivalent to pulling the power cable.
The guest OS is not given a chance to shut down cleanly; data loss or
filesystem corruption is possible. Prefer `shutdownVirtualMachine`.

VMInvalidState.description: Operation not valid for the current VM state

InternalError.description: Internal server error (no internal details are exposed)

bridgeName.description: Host bridge to attach to (required when mode is bridge).

cidr.description: Subnet for nat/isolated modes (required for those modes).

type.description: Only directory pools are supported for now

targetPath.description: Absolute host path; created if missing

VMState.description:
- running: powered on and operational
- stopped: powered off
- shutting-down: graceful shutdown in progress
- starting: power-on in progress

isoId.description: Optional ISO from the library to attach as install media (CD-ROM, first boot device).

usedBytes.description: Space currently allocated for this disk on the host (the backing volume's allocation, not the guest filesystem usage). Null when the hypervisor cannot report it.

VmMetrics.description: Point-in-time resource utilization of a running virtual machine. The whole object is absent while the VM is not running. Individual fields are null when the host cannot report them (e.g. no balloon driver / guest agent, or a first sample with no previous sample to diff against). Values are computed by the hypervisor provider, which is allowed to keep a short-lived sampling cache per VM.

cpuPercent.description: CPU utilization relative to the VM's allocated vCPUs.

memoryUsedBytes.description: Guest memory currently in use. Null unless the guest balloon driver or agent reports it.

networkRxBytesPerSecond.description: Inbound network throughput across all interfaces. Null until a second sample is available to compute a rate.

networkTxBytesPerSecond.description: Outbound network throughput across all interfaces. Null until a second sample is available to compute a rate.

sampledAt.description: When the underlying sample was taken.
